messages:
alex: FYI I'm seeing a recurring pattern of DNS SERVFAILs from our eu-west recursive forwarder (edge-recursive-1) that correlate with short burst failures in model-serving pods. :eyes:

mouna: timing? is it constant or spikes?

alex: spikes every ~5m for ~20-40s. UDP queries drop, we see a sharp rise in DNS over TCP fallback and increased latency. kube-proxy logs show pods failing hostname lookups. quick grep from pilot logs:
```
2026-03-17T15:12:03Z ERR lookup failed: query="models-internal.redwood" error=SERVFAIL upstream=edge-recursive-1:53 proto=udp
2026-03-17T15:12:04Z WARN falling back to tcp upstream=edge-recursive-1:53 proto=tcp
```

jin: do we have per-client ratelimits on the forwarder? could be RRL/ratelimit kicking in. I remember edge-recursive-1 got a config change last week.

alex: yes, it looks like unbound/bind-style rate limiting. config excerpt from forwarding node:
```
# edge-recursive-1
rate-limit: 150
per-client: 10
```
we're hitting per-client buckets from the node-local caches and k8s nodes aggregate queries -> bursts exceed per-client and start returning SERVFAIL.

mouna: hmm. negative caching also hurts — SERVFAILs get cached by clients for short negative-ttl and then we pile up again. do we know which clients are the biggest hitters?

alex: prometheus qps top talkers show kube-dns-proxy + kv-cache warmups (model shards) are the top ones. large fanout at rollout times.

ops-oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) route problem nodes to alternate forwarder (edge-recursive-2) via kube-dns configmap split, 2) temporarily enlarge per-client bucket on forwarder, 3) add local unbound on nodes for prefix caching. Which do we want first?

jin: route to alternate forwarder first — quick patch to coredns ConfigMap can change stubDomains. I'll open a small rollout. :+1:

mouna: in parallel can we bump per-client to 50? that should stop the short blips while we fix the root cause. alex, can you push the change to the unbound/bind template?

alex: pushing a change to increase per-client to 50 now. also adding a short note to ops runbook about negative TTL tuning (reduce negative caching to 10s for SERVFAILs).

ops-oncall: also track UDP fragmentation/EDNS size. If forwarder starts sending larger responses and EDNS is misconfigured upstream, we see UDP fail and TCP fallback which blows connections. Quick test command:
```
dig @edge-recursive-1 google.com +noedns +notcp
# and
dig @edge-recursive-1 google.com +tcp
```
we should compare failure modes.

jin: opened PR to coredns to add fallback forwarder and updated ConfigMap in staging. rolling to prod with canary 10% now.

alex: sanity check logs after the change show the spike windows shrink and tcp fallback count drops ~70% for the last 20m. still keeping monitoring alert for >10s consecutive SERVFAILs.

mouna: next steps: longer-term we should add a node-local caching unbound on all GPU nodes (short ttl for negative responses), and add per-pod resolver rotation so single node fanout doesn't hit same per-client bucket upstream. I'll add to infra backlog.

ops-oncall: also file a ticket with DNS provider to review RRL defaults — they applied a global change recently, might be related.

sre-bot: incident created: DNS-2026-0317-01 forwarded to eng-infra, severity: medium.

alex: thanks everyone, leaving the per-client bump and coredns fallback in place for 6h and will validate no regressions. report back if you see any new SERVFAIL windows.
